required_outcomes: Recognises that the tenant now reports a different fault (banging and movement on the spin, a small leak at the door) and that the 60°C heating repair is working, rather than treating it as the earlier repair failing.

Raises or reopens a job for the new fault and either asks the landlord (Mercer) to approve an appliance engineer call-out, or asks Lantern Services whether the problem could relate to their visit days earlier (the machine was pulled out for the repair), with the landlord told in either case.
Replies to the tenant that the new problem is being looked into, with practical advice to keep the machine out of use (or turn off its water supply) while it leaks, without inventing a visit date.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the tenant one quick question (for example whether the machine was pushed back level after the engineer's visit, or for a photo of the leak) alongside raising the job, as long as the job is not held up waiting for the answer.
Treating it as a linked return visit by Lantern at no charge, provided this is put to Lantern as a question about their visit and the landlord is not told the earlier repair failed.
positive_behaviours: Mentions the recent heating-element wiring repair and its date when writing to the landlord, so he sees the full history of the appliance.
Records the new fault and its start date (Saturday 2 March) in the case notes.
Notes that the earlier £75.11 invoice is for a repair the tenant says is now working.
red_flags: Telling the landlord the earlier repair has failed or that the heating fault has come back.
Escalating to a human when the next step is a routine approval request or contractor query.
prohibited_actions: Instructing a chargeable call-out for the new fault without the landlord's approval.
Closing the request or replying to the tenant that nothing more will be done.
critical_failures: Leaving the tenant's new report unactioned with the case closed.
